name: CUDABeaver
description: CUDABeaver is a benchmark of 203 reproducible CUDA debugging cases for evaluating LLM-based automated kernel repair. Each task starts from a real failing CUDA workspace (broken kernel + raw error log + native build/test harness) and is labeled with one of 5 curation-time error-category buckets (compile_error, logic_error, memory_crash, perf_broken, timeout), collapsed from an 8-category per-iteration classifier (compile_error, integration, environment_dependency, illegal_memory_access, out_of_memory, timeout, functional_correctness, perf_broken). The corpus spans 12 kernel families across two tiers: NVIDIA-library/curated (KernelBench, CUDA samples, CUDABench, cuSOLVER, cuSPARSE, cuBLAS, cuFFT, ThunderKittens, LayerNorm) and frontier-kernel (CUTLASS, FlashAttention v2). Designed for measuring debugging ability distinct from kernel generation, with support for performance-preservation evaluation. Companion dataset of the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track paper "CUDABeaver: Benchmarking LLM-Based Automated CUDA Debugging".

field.name: error_category
field.description: One of: compile_error, logic_error, memory_crash, perf_broken, timeout

field.name: difficulty
field.description: Coarse difficulty label carried in the task metadata: one of easy, medium, hard. This is not the empirical L1-L5 tier used in the paper.

field.name: broken_start_hash
field.description: First 16 hex chars of sha256(broken_start file contents)

field.name: path
field.description: Relative path under data/ to this instance's per-file directory; broken_start.{cu,py,h}, reference.{cu,py}, prompt.txt, input.json (build/test commands), instance.json, and testbench/ live there.

rai:dataCollection: Broken CUDA kernels were collected by sampling iter-1 outputs from frontier LLMs on a held-out set of CUDA programming tasks; outputs that exhibited compile-error, logic-error, memory-crash, perf-broken, or timeout failures were curated as instances. References are author-written or sourced from CUTLASS / FlashAttention / cuFFT / KernelBench upstreams.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual curation of LLM outputs + import from public open-source kernels
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Tasks where no LLM-generated broken_start exhibited a target failure category were excluded. 8 reference-unstable kernels were trimmed during initial curation.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw LLM completions are not redistributed (would re-identify the source frontier model). Only the curated broken_start code is included.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: Not applicable - no imputation. Missing testbench / reference for any task -> task excluded.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Source LLM outputs were only filtered for category match; no code rewriting beyond standardising file extensions and stripping comments that referenced the source LLM.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each broken_start is the unmodified LLM iter-1 output. Reference implementations are unmodified upstream code (CUTLASS, FlashAttention, cuFFT samples, ThunderKittens, KernelBench) or author-written for the curated CUDA programming pool.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each instance is annotated with: task_family, error_category (5 curation-time buckets, collapsed from an 8-category per-iteration classifier), and difficulty (coarse easy / medium / hard label from the task metadata). Annotation by deterministic classifier - no human labeling step.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom Python classifier (harness/classifier.py in companion code repo)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement not applicable: the classifier is a deterministic rule-based system built on nvcc exit codes, error-pattern regex, and PyTorch reference comparison. Categorization is reproducible exactly given the harness output. Rules were developed iteratively against a 50-instance development set spanning all 5 error categories.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Custom Python classifier; nvcc / KernelBench eval_kernel_against_ref for build+test-based category assignment
rai:dataBiases: (a) Source LLM bias: broken_starts inherit failure-mode distributions of source models, biased toward common LLM mistakes. (b) Domain bias: 12 task families, weighted toward CUDA C++ + KernelBench Python; under-represents OpenCL, ROCm, Triton. (c) Difficulty skew: harder tiers (L4-L5) cluster in compile_error / memory_crash; easier tiers (L1) dominate logic_error.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating LLM debugging capability on GPU kernels. Comparing test-time strategies. Studying feedback-richness, history-depth, few-shot exemplar effects.
rai:dataLimitations: Single-iteration debugging only - does not measure long-horizon (>5 round) repair. Main evaluation on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, with a replication on an NVIDIA H200 (Hopper). Not a measure of from-scratch kernel generation. Performance numbers are hardware-specific. License note: dataset curation is released under CC-BY 4.0; upstream-derived instances retain their original licenses (CUTLASS, FlashAttention v2: BSD-3-Clause; KernelBench, ThunderKittens: MIT). Per-instance license metadata is in instance.json.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Low risk. Benchmark contains only public-domain CUDA programming patterns. No personal data. Dual-use: improved LLM debugging could accelerate GPU code generation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. Dataset contains only kernel source code with no PII, no user-identifying content, no copyrighted text outside CC-licensed upstreams.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioned releases in the public GitHub repository https://github.com/UMN-APEX-Lab/CUDABeaver. Future versions on bug fixes or task-pool expansion. Maintained by the authors.
